name: Gavak
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

earlier_scan.source_named: Pick, Andrew. 2020. A Reconstruction of Proto-Northern Adelbert Phonology and Lexicon (PhD, UH Manoa) read in full: states stress data for these languages are 'minimal or nonexistent'; no Gavak stress statement.
earlier_scan.note: No stress description exists per Pick 2020; Gavak prosody undocumented.

sources.note: 9 references: Z'graggen 1968, 1969/1971, 1975a, 1975b, 1980 (x2), Pick 2020, Pick 2022, ISO CR 2012-091; doctypes overview/minimal/comparative/wordlist only; no descriptive source beyond Pick 2020.

sources.citation: TransNewGuinea.org, 'Gavak' (S. Greenhill ed.) and source record 'Pick (2019)'
sources.note: Only sources: Pick 2019 and Z'graggen 1980; retyped lexicon without stress marks.

sources.citation: Usher, Timothy (ed.). NewGuineaWorld: Gavak (wiki page, last modified 2024-06-25).
sources.note: Sources listed: Z'graggen 1980 (315 terms, pronouns) and Pick 2020: 164-183 grammar sketch (PDF pagination). Phonology paragraph restates Pick's 14 C / 5 V and phonotactics; no stress or accent statement.

sources.citation: Pick, Andrew. 2020. A reconstruction of Proto-Northern Adelbert phonology and lexicon. PhD dissertation, University of Hawai'i at Manoa. 485 pp.
sources.note: Sec. 1.5.1 'Stress' (pp. 31-32): stress described only for Mauwake, Pamosu, Usan; 'Unfortunately, the available data on stress in most languages are minimal or nonexistent'. Ch. 6 Gavak (author's own 2017-18 fieldwork, Dimir village; printed pp. 172ff, TOC 173-194): 6.1 phonemes (5 V, 14 C), 6.2 syllable (C)V(C) and word structure, 6.3 morphophonology -- no mention of stress, accent, tone or pitch anywhere in the chapter.

sources.citation: Pick, Andrew. 2019. Yamben: a previously undocumented language of Papua New Guinea. In M. Suzuki (ed.), 2018 Proceedings: Selected papers from the 22nd college-wide conference for students in LLL, 25-35. Honolulu: UH Manoa.
sources.note: Phonology section is about Yamben; 'Gabak' appears only in a five-language comparative wordlist table; nothing on Gavak stress.
Lists the Gildipasi documentation project (incl. Gavak) and the Kaipuleohone AP1 deposit; no separate Gavak phonology paper or talk.

sources.citation: ISO 639-3 Registration Authority. 2012. Change Request 2012-091 (submitted by Adam Boyd, SIL-PNG): rename dmc 'Dimir' to 'Gavak'; adopted 2013-01-23.
sources.note: Name-change rationale only (Dimir is a tree name; speakers call the language Gavak); no linguistic description, no published sources cited.

sources.citation: Z'graggen, J. A. 1980. A comparative word list of the Northern Adelbert Range languages, Madang Province, Papua New Guinea. Pacific Linguistics D-31. Canberra: ANU. (Dimir = E1)
sources.note: Intro sec. 7: transcription 'semi-phonemic; i.e. apparently non-contrastive phonetic details are omitted'; Dimir entries carry vowel-length marks (mE:rnE:, kunE:t) but no stress marks; nothing on stress.

sources.citation: Z'graggen, J. A. 1975. The Madang-Adelbert Range Sub-Phylum. In Wurm (ed.), PL C-38, 569-612.
sources.note: Dimir population (1,668), 'family-level isolate... overt number marking on nouns', comparative pronoun rows; nothing on phonology or stress.

sources.citation: Z'graggen, J. A. 1971. Classificatory and typological studies in languages of the Madang District. Pacific Linguistics C-19. Canberra: ANU. (Dimir = language 21)
sources.note: Sec. 2.22.13 'The Dimir Language' (villages, first listed by Kasprus 1942 / Capell 1954 'Boskien', cognate %, number marking, one possessive class, object incorporation, preposed negation); sec. 2.22.15 Isumrud Stock segmental typology; sec. 2.22.8 (p. 73) Adelbert Range Phylum: 'None of the languages appears to be tonal'; sec. 3.56.2.2 + Illustration 27 (pp. 152-153) Dimir verb structure. Nothing on stress.
Consonant and vowel tables taken from Pick 2020; no statement on stress, accent or tone.
